claims.explanation: PP-2 is a Src-family kinase inhibitor, and its selective killing pattern tracks with dependence on Src/FAK signaling rather than any single lineage. Sensitive lines are enriched for RAS/RTK pathway activation (KRAS, BRAF, NRAS, NF1, EGFR, ALK) and PTEN loss, which can increase Src/FAK and PI3K signaling, while resistant lines often have intact or alternative survival signaling. The virtual-cell similarity to PP-1 and PI3K/mTOR inhibitors supports a Src-to-PI3K/FAK mechanism.

features.basis: PTEN loss releases PI3K/FAK signaling that Src inhibitors can block; enriched in sensitive lines
RAS-driven lines may depend on Src/FAK survival signaling; seen in sensitive gastric/colorectal/pancreas lines
BRAF-mutant melanoma/endometrial lines are among sensitive; MAPK/Src crosstalk
NF1 loss activates RAS-MAPK and may increase Src dependence
EGFR activation can signal through Src/FAK; EGFR-mutant lung line is sensitive
ALK fusion/activation may engage Src-family signaling; ALK-mutant mesothelioma line is sensitive
Higher Src expression/activity predicts response to Src inhibition
FAK is a Src substrate and mediator of survival; high FAK signaling predicts sensitivity
PIK3CA-mutant lines are more frequent among resistant lines, suggesting PI3K activation can bypass Src inhibition
ARID1A mutations appear enriched in resistant lines, possibly reflecting chromatin-mediated survival
TP53 mutation is common in both groups but slightly more frequent in resistant lines; weak evidence
CDKN2A loss appears in several resistant lines; weak evidence
